title: How to Plan for a Child’s Higher Education (U.S. vs. International Costs)
description: Comparing 529 plans, studying abroad, and ROI on degrees.
content:
The cost of college in the US has spiraled out of control, with private universities topping $90,000 per year. For new parents, the projected cost of a degree in 2040 could exceed $500,000. This reality is forcing families to look at alternatives: public in-state universities, community college transfers, and increasingly, international universities. Did you know a degree in Germany or the UK can cost 50-80% less than a US degree? This guide compares the savings strategies for domestic vs. global education.

Key Takeaways

  • The 529 Flexibility: 529 plans can be used for hundreds of international universities (e.g., Oxford, McGill, University of Melbourne). You aren't locked into US schools.
  • The Cost Delta: A 4-year degree at a US private college might cost $350k. A 3-year degree (standard in UK/Europe) might cost $60k total. Geographic arbitrage is a massive wealth hack.
  • Room & Board Rule: In the US, tuition is the killer. In Europe, tuition is cheap/free, but you must pay cash for Room & Board (Living costs). 529s cover both.
  • The 'Superfunding' Move: You can contribute 5 years of gifts ($90k) to a 529 at once to jumpstart compounding.

Why It Matters (US Context)

US student loan debt is a unique crisis ($1.7 Trillion). Saving aggressively in a 529 plan reduces the reliance on loans. Recent laws allow unused 529 funds (up to $35k) to roll into a Roth IRA, removing the fear of over-saving.

Domestic vs. International Math

Scenario: Saving for a child born in 2025.

Path A: Private US University (2043)

  • Projected Cost: $400,000+.
  • Savings Required: $800/month for 18 years (at 7% return).
  • Risk: Degree ROI might not justify the cost.

Path B: In-State Public (2043)

  • Projected Cost: $150,000.
  • Savings Required: $300/month.
  • Risk: State budget cuts raising tuition faster than inflation.

Path C: European University (English Program)

  • Tuition: ~$5,000/year (International Student rate in places like Germany/Netherlands).
  • Living: $15,000/year.
  • Degree Length: 3 Years.
  • Total Cost: $60,000.
  • Verdict: You could cash flow this without saving much at all.

The 529 Execution

  1. Open Early: Open the account before the baby is born (in your name), then transfer to the baby. Time matters.
  2. State Tax Benefit: Check if your state offers a tax deduction. If so, use your state's plan. If not, use Utah or Nevada (low fees).
  3. International List: Go to savingforcollege.com and check the 'Federal School Code List'. If a foreign school has a code, you can use 529 money there tax-free.
  4. The 'Grandparent' Strategy: Ask grandparents to contribute to a 529 instead of buying toys. Under new FAFSA rules, grandparent-owned 529s no longer hurt financial aid eligibility.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if my kid doesn't go to college?

1. Change beneficiary to sibling.
2. Roll $35k to Roth IRA.
3. Pay 10% penalty + tax to withdraw cash (still better than a brokerage account if held long enough).

Can I use 529 for flight tickets?

No. Travel is not a 'Qualified Education Expense'. You must pay for flights to Europe out of pocket. Room, Board, Books, and Tuition are covered.

Is the IB Diploma helpful?

Yes. If aiming for international schools, the International Baccalaureate (IB) is widely recognized and often grants college credit, shortening the degree time.
